Good morning, everyone. Ray Collins. Two minutes about last week, and then we start. It rained for five days and we lost three of them. I know. On Tuesday the water came down the ramp, one truck got stuck at the entrance, and six of you took shovels and spent the whole morning on it. On Wednesday I made the decision to close the lower area, and some of you were not happy with me. At eleven o'clock that area was under water. I am not saying I was right. I am saying we had nobody down there. Thursday and Friday we covered the machines, we went through the old reports, and we made a new schedule. And here is the good news from the office: the delay is three days, not seven. Nothing is broken. Now, this week.

Hi Giovanna, it is Karen. I saw your message about the rain and I laughed, sorry. Last March we had exactly the same week here in London. It started on a Monday, and by Wednesday there was a small flood in the lower tunnel. My supervisor said one thing only: everybody out. So we went up, we made tea, and we waited. I took photographs of the water for the report, and honestly they are the best photographs I have. Two things I learned that week. First, a storm is never a surprise here, so we always cover the machines on Friday afternoon, every Friday, even in July. Second, the delay was six days and nobody lost their job. Send me a photo of your mud. Talk soon.

On Monday the rain started at five in the morning. On Tuesday a truck got stuck in the mud at the entrance. On Wednesday Ray made the decision and closed the lower area. On Thursday the crew took plastic sheets and covered the machines. On Saturday the sun came back and the news was good.
